correspondence.component_scope: Chosen short northward opening and first eastward connection
correspondence.finding: The original municipal drainage network depicts the short headward feeder near the Samaúma and Ywauká settlement setting and its connection into the eastward course. The selected opening is covered at ordinary corridor scale. Neither nearby settlement labels nor the system's downstream hydronym are assigned as a separate name for this initial feeder.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastward inland feeder and intervening tributary joins
correspondence.finding: The original shows the continuous eastward drainage corridor north of the Samaúma/Paraitkur settlement belt, with its intervening north- and south-side tributary connections. Its bend sequence and eastward connection to the Cumurumã–Kumarumã area correspond to the selection. This is not inferred merely from membership in the indigenous territory or Uaçá basin.

correspondence.component_scope: Cumurumã approach, material junction and Kumarumã northward turn
correspondence.finding: The municipal original depicts the selected eastward arrival at the main northbound watercourse in the Cumurumã/Karibuene setting and its northeast-to-north continuation past Aruatu and Kumarumã. The park-plan prose independently associates Kumarumã with travel on Rio Uaçá and describes the named river's west-east course turning south-north near the park. The southern unselected continuation is not added to the selected geometry.

correspondence.component_scope: Long northbound channel through the lowland and lateral lake/tributary setting
correspondence.finding: The municipal original continuously maps the selected northward channel east of Igarapé Tipoca and west of Lago Maruani and the separate Cassiporé river. Its small western lake-and-channel junction and lateral tributaries are visible. The selection remains in the northbound river corridor; it does not cross Lago Maruani, and the map's Maruani connection toward Cassiporé is not substituted for the selected route. The park-plan maps and prose corroborate the regional Uaçá lowland/fluvio-estuarine setting.

correspondence.component_scope: Northwest turn, junction with western approach and stage-3/stage-2 continuity
correspondence.finding: The municipal map depicts the selected northwest turn into a larger channel north of Flexa and the distinct western approach passing the Tipoca/Urubu setting. The selected junction and continuation through the first stored fragment boundary are continuous on the source. The western branch's local labels are not treated as alternate names for the full selected upper route.

correspondence.component_scope: Northwest-trending named trunk to the next fragment boundary
correspondence.finding: Repeated Rio Uaçá labels occur on the mapped trunk followed by this complete fragment. The source shows its northwest progression, side inflows, Posto Uaçá/Encruzo setting and continuity toward the next fragment. Rio Caripi and the western Oiapoque channel are geographically separate and are not substituted for this trunk.

correspondence.component_scope: Stage-1 lower Uaçá corridor and actual stored endpoint
correspondence.finding: The entire final fragment corresponds to the mapped lower Rio Uaçá, east of the Jumina peninsula and the separately labelled Rio Oiapoque. The source shows the actual selected endpoint within this lower river/estuarine corridor, with Uaçá continuing farther downstream into the broader receiving-water setting. The municipal overview and park-plan cartography show that downstream Oyapock/Atlantic context. No open-ocean mouth is assigned to the stored endpoint, and no unselected extension is added merely because the model terminal class says sea.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen northern opening before the mapped Macusa course
correspondence.finding: The selection begins northwest of the northern end of the natural-watercourse line that subsequently carries the Río Macusa label. The first two stored parts and the beginning of the third extend beyond that mapped line. Neither the IGM waterbody rendering nor the acquired coastal municipal plan explains this short headward interval. Its source-to-channel correspondence and component name remain unestablished; no natural-source location or absence of a real channel is inferred.

correspondence.component_scope: Mapped Macusa descent and northern tributary junctions
correspondence.finding: After the unsupported opening, the selected southeastern and southern course follows the mapped channel labeled Río Macusa. The mapped northeastern tributary and other eastern approaches enter separately. The selection continues south and southwest to the Río Blanco joining setting and toward the westward receiving course; it does not follow the Río Blanco branch upstream. Individual bends are generalized without a missing intermediate through-link at ordinary corridor scale.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper westward Ajatama course and southern receiving approach
correspondence.finding: The selected route turns west along the explicitly labeled Río Ajatama corridor, passing the separately labeled Q. Chacia approach and continuing to the connected southern tributary setting. Municipal plan prose independently states that Ajatama approaches from the north and Caritaya from the south to form Camarones. This supports the receiving-system relationship, without fixing an exact hydronym-transition vertex. The selected route remains on the northern/westward river corridor and does not ascend the southern Caritaya approach or traverse its separately situated reservoir.

correspondence.component_scope: Westward receiving course and Achecagua–Saguara approaches
correspondence.finding: The westward selection follows the connected main drainage past the separate southeastern Q. Achecagua approach and the northern Q. Saguara network. Both the tributary junctions and the westward continuation are visible in the original IGM raster. The distinct tributary names are not aliases for the selected mainstem, and the selected stored-part boundaries do not define name boundaries.

correspondence.component_scope: Middle southwestward Camarones corridor and northern Umayani approach
correspondence.finding: The selected river bends southwest and west through the continuous receiving corridor. The IGM source labels Río Camarones on this course and shows the separate Q. Umayani approach from the north. The selection remains on the common western river, generalizing bends through the tributary-junction setting. The municipal plan uses Humayami in its regional description; no formal equivalence between these source spellings is adjudicated.

correspondence.component_scope: Long lower southwestward river corridor
correspondence.finding: The selection follows the continuously depicted southwestern Camarones course toward the Cuya area, with ordinary lateral simplification of its bends. The southern Humallani, Cutijmalla and Chiza drainage network remains separate until its downstream receiving junction. No intermediate lake, salar or reservoir is required to connect the selected mainstem portions shown here.

correspondence.component_scope: Chiza junction and Cuya receiving setting
correspondence.finding: The selected route enters the lower junction from the northeast and continues southwest along the mapped Río Camarones. Q. de Chiza approaches separately from the east and southeast. The municipal plan identifies Cuya at this confluence, and its inspected local imagery depicts the joined alluvial valley, active vegetation and neighboring dry channel terrain. This accounts for the selected junction corridor without asserting a particular contemporary channel thread or perennial flow in Chiza.

correspondence.component_scope: Actual selected coastal terminal and lower wetland
correspondence.finding: The final selected portion follows the lower mapped Camarones corridor to its coastal ending. The municipal plan’s inspected mouth imagery places the vegetated river/wetland corridor at the narrow valley opening onto the Pacific, distinguishes the neighboring Caleta Camarones and pier setting, and identifies the river-mouth wetland. Together these sources account for the actual selected terminal at ordinary coastal-corridor scale. The selected tip is not adopted as a surveyed present shoreline crossing, a current open-mouth channel, or a tidal limit.

correspondence.component_scope: Lake, reservoir, salar, wetland and managed-passage scope
correspondence.finding: The whole-corridor IGM waterbody rendering depicts a separate surface southeast of the selected upper westward course, outside the selected route. No selected lake, reservoir or salar traversal is established. The acquired municipal plan documents a wetland on the lower Camarones mouth corridor and regional Caritaya-reservoir context; it does not place a reservoir on this northern selected route. The natural-watercourse and surface views do not establish every small impoundment, all irrigation works or present wetness. No selected engineered transfer is assumed. correspondence.component_scope: Upper Rio Palmeira and northward continuation to the Preguiças joining setting
correspondence.finding: The Urbano Santos original traces the selected valley through Formiga, Angicalinho, Bom Fim, Bom Jesus, Areias, Santa Maria, Boa União and Pau d’Arco toward Palmira and Jabuti. It labels the upper course Rio Palmeira. The overlapping Barreirinhas original labels Rio Palmeira near Palmira and depicts its connection into the Preguiças course; a separate eastern Rio Preguiças de Cabeceira approach is not substituted for the selected western opening.

The Barreirinhas map repeatedly labels the continuing selected corridor Rio Preguiças and traces it past Maracujá, Vassoura, Palmeira dos Pereiras, Prata and the lower valley. correspondence.component_scope: Lower river approach through Barreirinhas and fragment join

The stage-three fragment ends in the same mapped urban river corridor where the stage-two selection continues. The fragment boundary is not interpreted as a natural name boundary.

correspondence.component_scope: Barreirinhas to the broad Preguiças estuarine and wetland corridor
correspondence.finding: The municipal original connects Barreirinhas through Laranjeiras and the broad island/wetland complex including Ilha do Meio toward the lower Preguiças estuary. Its mapped water and marsh corridor supports the selected sequence at regional estuarine scale. The wide tidal complex is retained as such; the simplified selection is not asserted to select a surveyed bank, a particular current tidal thread, or a separate lake hydronym. Costa’s independently authored estuary study corroborates the named Preguiças tidal/dune/mangrove setting.

correspondence.component_scope: Actual selected terminal extension from lower estuary to the Atlantic
correspondence.finding: The initial part of the final stored part lies in the lower Preguiças corridor. Its final northeastward extension reaches the Atlantic across the coastal barrier east of the mapped estuary rather than following the mapped continuation north toward Mandacaru, Caburé and the inlet. The municipal map depicts a dune/barrier strip along that connection. Costa’s location image and inlet figures show the northern inlet and migrating spit, but do not establish the selected southeastern crossing. The source endpoint and the actual rendered ending were both considered; neither the source endpoint nor the unselected northern mouth replaces the selected ending.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen glacial opening and upper White River receiving connection
correspondence.finding: The chosen opening occupies Emmons Glacier on Mount Rainier’s northeast flank and follows its lower-glacier/outwash corridor toward White River near the Inter Fork approach and campground. The map distinguishes the glacier, adjoining Inter Fork and valley channel; NPS independently states that Emmons meltwater is the White River source. The initial ice-covered portion is described as glacier drainage, not renamed as a continuous exposed river or assigned a precise natural source.
correspondence.component_name: Emmons Glacier drainage to White River

correspondence.component_scope: Upper White River eastward and northward bend
correspondence.finding: The selected eastward valley and northward turn follow the labelled White River past the Fryingpan Creek receiving setting and along the park valley toward Silver Springs. The incoming valley creeks and nearby lakes are mapped as separate side features; no selected lake-to-lake transfer is needed.

correspondence.component_scope: Northern White River valley and major upstream joins
correspondence.finding: The White River continues north through the Huckleberry Creek receiving setting and the West Fork White River junction, then reaches the Greenwater River confluence. Repeated labels and continuous mapped channel correspond to the selected parts. The West Fork and Greenwater are incoming named branches rather than alternative names for the selected main corridor.

correspondence.component_scope: Westward White River through forested middle valley
correspondence.finding: The route follows White River west from Greenwater across the middle valley and tributary joins, including the Clearwater River receiving setting. The repeated river labels, continuous channel and matching valley turns establish the selected through-corridor.

correspondence.component_scope: White River through the Mud Mountain valley and constricted outlet
correspondence.finding: The detailed original map continuously depicts White River across the wetland-rich valley, around Mud Mountain and through the constricted western outlet into the downstream river. There is no missing or ambiguous selected through-link at ordinary corridor scale. Explicit dam/reservoir naming and storage/operation details are unverified because the optional project and county pages supplied no readable body; this is a management-detail limit, not a geographic material gap.

correspondence.component_scope: White River from Red Creek and Buckley into the incised lowland valley
correspondence.finding: The selected corridor continues past the Red Creek and Boise Creek receiving settings, Buckley and the valley adjoining the Muckleshoot Reservation. Mapped side channels and the separate Lake Tapps waterbody are distinguished from the White River main passage; the selection does not traverse Lake Tapps.

correspondence.component_scope: Auburn bend, southward White River, Sumner junction and mainstem-fragment seam
correspondence.finding: The selected route follows the White River bend south of Auburn, turns south along the western side of the Lake Tapps upland through Pacific toward Sumner, and enters the labelled Puyallup River. Both selected fragments meet in this lower receiving corridor. The selected route continues down Puyallup, not into the separately mapped Green River or Lake Tapps. The generalized fragment seam is not used as a surveyed hydronym boundary.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Puyallup River across Puyallup and Fife lowlands
correspondence.finding: Direct labels and a continuous mapped river establish the westward and northwestward selected lower reach through the Puyallup/Fife lowland to the Tacoma approach, including the depicted lowland side-channel joins. The long upstream White River reach retains its own name.

correspondence.component_scope: Tacoma port channel and actual coastal terminal
correspondence.finding: The final selected reach follows the port-adjacent Puyallup River into the labelled Puyallup Waterway at Commencement Bay, part of Puget Sound. The surrounding Milwaukee, Sitcum, Blair and Middle waterways are separate mapped port features. Ordinary terminal-corridor correspondence is established without requiring the generalized endpoint to match an exact bank, tidal shoreline or surveyed mouth vertex.
